title: Weather and zero-shot forecasting models: backtest results for GB electricity demand (part 1 of 2)
claim: In a preregistered 960-day day-ahead backtest on GB national demand, giving Chronos-2, Timestral-209M, TimesFM 2.5 and a weekly-lag regression the same honestly timed weather forecasts cut error for all of them, and the models' advantage over the regression largely disappears once the regression has weather.
why_relevant: Same design as our benchmark (zero-shot foundation models against a lag regression with identical forecast-regime temperature) on national hourly load, day-ahead rather than week-ahead.

title: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models for Load Forecasting Under Covariate Uncertainty
claim: Across three load datasets, Chronos-2 is the most accurate zero-shot and fine-tuned when future covariates are available or well forecast, but degrades as covariate forecasts get noisier, where TimesNet is more robust.
why_relevant: Directly tests the oracle-versus-forecast weather gap for covariate-aware foundation models on electric load, the split our two regimes report.

title: PJM Cold-Spell Calibration Benchmark: When Cold-Spell Calibration Fails to Transfer
claim: In a pre-registered benchmark over four PJM extreme-cold events, 90% load forecast intervals lose coverage inside the events and no conformal calibrator chosen without the target event restores it.
why_relevant: PJM load with temperature-driven extremes and a frozen protocol; day-ahead and probabilistic rather than week-ahead point forecasts.

title: Assessing Covariate-Informed Grid Load Forecasting with a Time-Series Foundation Model
claim: On ISO New England and ENTSO-E load, Chronos-2 with exogenous inputs gains substantially from task-specific fine-tuning and is strong at short horizons against task-specific deep models.
why_relevant: Chronos-2 with covariates on US ISO load is our primary comparison's model on a neighbouring system.

title: Timestral
claim: Mistral released four open-weights probabilistic forecasting models (5M to 209M parameters) that accept known-future covariates and says the two largest rank first and second among zero-shot models on GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench.
why_relevant: A covariate-aware model already listed as runnable with temperature in our spec; its weights fall inside the scored window.

title: TimesFM 3.0
claim: Google released TimesFM 3.0, a 330M-parameter zero-shot model with native multivariate forecasting and past and future covariate support; the weights carry a non-commercial licence.
why_relevant: A new covariate-capable release that FoundationForecast wraps with native exogenous support, so it can take our temperature series.

title: t0: A Time-Series Foundation Model for Forecasting with Context
claim: The open-weights t0 family conditions forecasts on past and known-future covariates without retraining, places third on GIFT-Eval and fev-bench, and reports that known-future covariates add about 6 points of skill across 30 tasks.
why_relevant: A known-future-covariate model that FoundationForecast runs natively, with an hourly electricity-demand backtest among its own evidence.

title: How Far Does Zero-Shot Go? A Leakage-Aware Evaluation of TimesFM 3 on Post-Release, Multivariate and Controlled Data
claim: Under a protocol frozen before the test data existed, TimesFM 3 has about 16% lower MASE than a classical ensemble on post-release data including electricity load, leads Chronos-2 by about 5%, and its 80% intervals cover about 70%.
why_relevant: Post-release evaluation on load addresses the training-overlap risk our receipts must state for every foundation model.

title: A Benchmark for Electrical Load Forecasting Across Grid Levels: Time-Series Transformers Outperform Established Methods
claim: On control-area, feeder and end-consumer load data, Transformer models cut short-term forecast error by roughly 7 to 11% against established methods, while zero-shot Chronos-2 is competitive on two datasets but misses special events on the control-area data.
why_relevant: Includes a transmission-operator control area, the aggregation level closest to a PJM zone, with Chronos-2 as a zero-shot row.

title: Peak-Aware Short-Term Load Forecasting Across Distribution Grid Aggregation Levels
claim: On UK and Swiss distribution data, Chronos-2 has the lowest error in high-demand periods at all three aggregation levels, about 20 to 51% below LightGBM and XGBoost.
why_relevant: Chronos-2 against gradient boosting on electric load, both of which are rows on our leaderboard; distribution level and short horizon.

title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Time Series Foundation Models for Electrical Load Forecasting
claim: Across four load aggregation levels, pretrained Moirai and Chronos-2 beat seasonal naive and XGBoost baselines, and rank-16 LoRA on Moirai Large lowers normalised MAE by about 7.5% while updating about 1% of the weights.
why_relevant: Electric load with a Chronos-2 row; the headline is about fine-tuning, which our zero-shot benchmark does not do.

title: Systematic Evaluation of TabPFN-TS and Chronos-2 for Zero-Shot Heat Load Forecasting in District Heating Networks
claim: For hourly 24-hour heat load forecasts in two German networks with ambient temperature as covariate, zero-shot TabPFN-TS and Chronos-2 both beat trained baselines over a full year, under perfect weather with a separate forecast-weather sensitivity run.
why_relevant: Hourly energy series with temperature as a known-future input and both an oracle and a forecast weather run, mirroring our two regimes.

title: Machine Learning and Time-Series Foundation Models for Day-Ahead Electricity Forecasting in a University Building
claim: On 57 test days for one building, TimesFM 3.0 with covariates has the lowest day-ahead error (about 43% below weekly seasonal naive) but no clear advantage over XGBoost, and covariates help mainly on holidays.
why_relevant: Hourly electric load with weather covariates and TimesFM 3.0; a single building, a short test window and observed weather limit the match.

title: EnergyBench: a live, gate-aligned benchmark of day-ahead forecasts for European power markets
claim: A live daily benchmark scores foundation models and LightGBM on day-ahead price, wind, solar and load for six European zones, all on the same weather inputs frozen before the market gate.
why_relevant: Same-inputs, no-lookahead comparison of foundation models with a tree baseline on load, day-ahead and European rather than week-ahead PJM.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: pl-forecast-bench: a leakage-checked forecasting benchmark for the Polish power system
claim: A benchmark for Polish wind, solar, demand and price at 15-minute resolution fixes data, publication-time rules, a 12-month test year and reference models including zero-shot foundation models, with tests that detect look-ahead leakage.
why_relevant: National demand forecasting with archived weather forecasts and explicit as-of rules, the same discipline as our forecast regime.

title: Combining Weather Forecast Aggregation and State-Space Models for Adaptive Probabilistic Electricity Load Forecasting
claim: On French national load, an adaptive additive model with state-space updates forecasts better, especially in the tails, when it combines weather forecasts from several providers instead of one.
why_relevant: A regression-family load model fed forecast weather, relevant to how our temperature-only regression behaves in the forecast regime.

title: The Hidden Look-Ahead: Point-in-Time Leakage in Electricity Market Data
claim: Matching 128,656 archived weather forecast runs to GB auction gates shows that choosing the latest run issued before the gate usually picks a run not yet published at that time, with accuracy effects from -9% to +24%.
why_relevant: Bears on whether lead-matched archived forecasts in our forecast regime were really available at the Monday 00:00 issue time.

title: Zero-shot time-series foundation models against the Khepri v1.5 baselines for 96-hour carbon-intensity forecasts in nine Nordic bidding zones: a preregistered comparison
claim: In a preregistered comparison over 361 origins in 2025, univariate Timestral and Chronos-2 have about 1 to 1.3 points lower MAPE than SARIMA and gradient boosting baselines for 96-hour hourly carbon intensity, while a 14-origin post-release holdout is inconclusive.
why_relevant: Hourly zonal energy series at a multi-day horizon with a preregistered design and two of our runnable models, without covariates.

title: On the Encoding of Calendar Features in Covariate-Informed Time Series Foundation Models
claim: Across four foundation models and nine socially driven datasets, how calendar covariates are encoded changes zero-shot MASE by up to about 10% on ordinary days and far more on holidays.
why_relevant: Our week-ahead load windows include holidays, and the covariate-aware models we run could take calendar inputs alongside temperature.

title: TimeH2O-v1
claim: H2O.ai released a roughly 108M-parameter zero-shot probabilistic model that accepts covariates and reports top GIFT-Eval and fev-bench scores, under a non-commercial licence.
why_relevant: Listed in our spec as a FoundationForecast model with native exogenous support, so it can be run with temperature.

title: Time Flies When You Parallelise: Pareto-efficient Time Series Foundation Models with Linear Recurrences
claim: The ci-proto family, built on linear state recurrences with cross-variate attention and future-known covariates, claims the best fev-bench score among foundation models and the whole accuracy-versus-cost frontier.
why_relevant: A new model taking known-future covariates whose low inference cost suits our CPU-only limit; not yet in FoundationForecast.

title: Timer-M1: A Multivariate Time Series Foundation Model via Learning Primitives
claim: Timer-M1, pretrained with channels assigned as targets, past-only covariates and known-future covariates, ranks first on FEV and TIME and second on GIFT-Eval among recent foundation models.
why_relevant: A pretrained model designed for known-future covariates such as temperature; whether weights are public is not stated.

title: Forecasting Associations, Not Interventions: A Preregistered Causal Audit of Covariate-Aware Time Series Foundation Models
claim: On a preregistered grid with known counterfactuals, Chronos-2, TiRex-2, TabPFN-TS and TimesFM-2.5 respond to a future covariate path with the associational rather than the causal effect, and more confounded than a regression.
why_relevant: Describes how covariate-aware models use a future input like temperature compared with a regression, on synthetic rather than load data.

title: A Later Test Set Is Not a New Domain: Pretraining Familiarity Survives a Contamination-Free Hold-Out
claim: On data published after every tested model, pretrained forecasters win 5 of 7 groups, and their advantage tracks how close the domain is to the pretraining corpus rather than seasonality or entropy.
why_relevant: Informs how to read our weeks-after-weights label: a post-release window removes contamination but not corpus familiarity.

title: Tabby: An Open Pretraining Recipe for Time Series Foundation Models
claim: Tabby is a 145M-parameter encoder-only probabilistic model released with its full training recipe, reporting competitive zero-shot results on GIFT-Eval and the TIME benchmark with contexts up to 8,192 points.
why_relevant: A new release in the FoundationForecast wrapper list, runnable on load history only.

title: IBM Granite PatchTST-FM-r2
claim: IBM's roughly 385M-parameter successor to PatchTST-FM-r1 claims the top GIFT-Eval rank among zero-shot models with a permissive open-source licence as of the end of August 2026.
why_relevant: A permissively licensed release in the FoundationForecast wrapper list, runnable on load history only.

title: Tafsut Univariate Base
claim: An MIT-licensed 105M-parameter univariate zero-shot model that outputs nine quantiles reports third place on GIFT-Eval CRPS among twelve compared models.
why_relevant: In the FoundationForecast wrapper list and runnable on load history only; it cannot take temperature.

title: Foundation or Formula? A Simulation-Based Comparison of Google's TimesFM-3 and Classical Time-Series Models
claim: On 7,200 simulated series under a pre-registered protocol with a 12-step horizon, neither TimesFM-3 nor classical methods dominate: TimesFM-3 is never more than 1.31 times the best method's error, while automatic ARIMA is 21 to 24% better on seasonal ARIMA data with enough cycles.
why_relevant: A pre-registered foundation-versus-classical comparison free of training overlap, on synthetic data and a short horizon.

title: Multi-horizon forecasting of national electricity demand in Türkiye: run records, forecasts and trained models
claim: An archive of 759 training runs with sealed test forecasts supports a study of multi-horizon national demand forecasting with calendar, holiday and temperature inputs; the record itself states no headline result.
why_relevant: National electricity demand at several horizons with temperature as an input, with sealed test forecasts.

title: Medium-Term Multi-Resolution Electric Load Forecasting using Economic Data and Foundation Model
claim: For French load forecast 1 to 48 months ahead with a tabular foundation model, selected economic covariates improve skill by about 20% over 2015 to 2025.
why_relevant: Electric load with a pretrained model and covariates, at monthly-to-yearly horizons far from our week ahead.

title: U.S. utility load forecasts filed on FERC Form 714, 2006–2025: forecast errors, weather-normalized outcomes, prediction intervals and capacity decision rules (code and data)
claim: Code and data evaluate about 13,700 utility-filed peak and energy forecasts against weather-normalised outcomes and build prediction intervals and capacity rules from past errors, with PJM's own forecasts among those examined.
why_relevant: US load forecast evaluation that touches PJM, at planning horizons of seasons to years rather than a week.

title: gridload-compact
claim: Two small quantile networks trained only on German SMARD net load report a lower mean MASE than every reference model on a 24-hour, 15-minute task over a seven-week test window and 14th of 46 in a later live shadow check.
why_relevant: National net-load forecasting up to 72 hours with calendar inputs only; self-evaluated and specific to one series.

title: Thaki-EnergyLoad-Forecaster-v0.1
claim: Three LightGBM models forecasting one meter's load 15 minutes, 1 hour and 24 hours ahead from its own history and calendar features beat the best simple baseline on a 2014 test period.
why_relevant: Electric load with a LightGBM model like our baseline, but meter-level, short-horizon and without weather.

title: BQEB ForecastBench: Benchmarking AI Models for Smart Grid Forecasting Using BQEB-Data v1
claim: A smart-grid forecasting benchmark reports results for simple baselines (linear regression, random forest, gradient boosting) on next-hour load.
why_relevant: A load benchmark, but one hour ahead with no foundation models or weather regime.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Analysis code for: Zero-shot time series foundation models for statistical postprocessing of weather forecasts: how much training data do they replace?
claim: A study compares zero-shot TimesFM-3 and Chronos-2, given the ensemble mean as covariate, with trained statistical postprocessing for 2 m temperature at 49 German stations out to 120 hours; the record does not state the result.
why_relevant: Concerns the quality of temperature forecasts, our required covariate in the forecast regime, rather than load itself.

title: Zero-Shot Forecasting of In-Situ Soil Moisture and Temperature with a Time-Series Foundation Model
claim: Zero-shot TimesFM on 27 field sensors beats rule-based baselines clearly at sub-daily horizons but falls behind them beyond a day, out to 168 hours, while a CatBoost model with weather covariates never wins overall.
why_relevant: Not an energy series, but it measures how a univariate foundation model holds up from one hour to our 168-hour horizon.

title: sktime v1.3.0
claim: sktime 1.3.0 adds forecaster wrappers for the TimeH2O and Tabby foundation models and updates its Timer-S1 wrapper.
why_relevant: A second route, besides FoundationForecast, to run new foundation models on our load series.

title: sktime v1.2.0
claim: sktime 1.2.0 adds forecaster wrappers for Tafsut, TimesFM 3, TiRex-2 and t0.
why_relevant: A second route to covariate-capable models (TimesFM 3, TiRex-2, t0) that we would otherwise run through FoundationForecast.

title: sktime v1.0.2
claim: sktime 1.0.2 adds forecaster wrappers for Moirai 2.0, Sundial and WindFM.
why_relevant: Wrappers for univariate foundation models that could be run on load history; the models themselves predate the window.

title: TabPFN-3.5: Technical Report
claim: The TabPFN-3.5 report says the tabular model's gains carry over to task-specific uses including stronger time-series forecasting, without giving forecasting benchmarks on its record page.
why_relevant: TabPFN-based forecasters take known-future covariates such as temperature; the forecasting claim here is thin.

title: forelint: lint your forecast backtests before you trust a score
claim: An open-source Python library checks forecasting backtests for leakage between related series, run-to-run noise and unsupported model comparisons, illustrated on M5 retail data where gradient boosting was 3.9% worse than a moving average.
why_relevant: Tooling for auditing a backtest like ours; it makes no claim about load forecasting.
